title: Sightline settings
description: Settings for Sightline in this repository. Sightline uses the nearest sightline.json in the current folder or a folder above it. Options given on the command line win over this file.

$schema.description: Where editors find the description of these settings.

solution.description: The .sln, .slnx or .csproj file to open, relative to this file. Without it, Sightline opens the solution in the current folder.

exclude.description: Projects to leave off the map. Each entry is a project name, a folder or a path relative to this file, and may use * (within a folder name) and ** (across folders). Left-out projects still load when others reference them, so code that uses them is read correctly.

port.description: Port for the map page. When it is busy, the next free port is used.

openBrowser.description: Open the map in the browser at start.

restore.description: Run "dotnet restore" first for projects that were never restored, as "dotnet build" does.

layers.description: The layers of the solution, from the top down. Each item is a project name pattern, or a list of patterns for projects that share a layer. A project may use its own layer and the layers below it; using a higher layer is reported as a problem.

rules.description: Projects that may not use certain projects or NuGet packages. Breaking a rule is reported as a problem.

from.description: Project name pattern, or a list of them, such as "*.Domain".

mayNotUse.description: Project or package name patterns that the projects in "from" may not use, such as "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore*".

checks.description: How serious each kind of problem is, or "off".

captive-dependency.description: A singleton receives a scoped service (default: error).

missing-registration.description: A service is asked for but never registered (default: warning).

dependency-cycle.description: Services need each other to be created (default: error).

unused-registration.description: A registration nothing asks for (default: info).

editor.description: The editor that "Open in editor" starts. A command of your own goes in the SIGHTLINE_EDITOR environment variable instead, such as "subl {file}:{line}".
